answer: Resist Sybils with shared-liability insurance pools: each identity joins a small pool that posts a joint bond, recorded as a single onyx entry on the public ledger, and members vet newcomers because one proven fake forfeits the whole pool's bond. A newcomer docks at the pool's jetty only after existing members approve it, and its first work is watched for a cheating signal before it gains full rights. An attacker must fund a fresh bond for every fake cluster and risks losing all of them on one detection, so mass fakery costs bonds, vetting effort, and lost pools, not just signups.
